config.title: Berlin Landmarks in 2 Hours - FAQ
config.subtitle: Straight answers for choosing a focused east or west landmark window in central Berlin.

items.q: Can I see Berlin's main landmarks in 2 hours?
items.a: You can have a useful central-Berlin landmark window in 2 hours, but not a complete city checklist. Choose either the Museum Island side or the Brandenburg Gate side, keep the walk outdoors by default, and add only one interior if it has a real purpose and current entry information.

items.q: Should I start at Museum Island or Brandenburg Gate?
items.a: Start near the side where you already are. Museum Island is the natural east window from Alexanderplatz or Hackescher Markt; Brandenburg Gate is the natural west window from Pariser Platz, the government quarter or Hauptbahnhof. Crossing between both sides is possible, but it usually turns a short visit into a transit-and-queue checklist.

items.q: Can I visit the Reichstag dome and Brandenburg Gate in the same 2 hours?
items.a: Only treat the dome as possible when you already have a confirmed visitor option. The Brandenburg Gate works well as an outdoor stop; the Reichstag dome needs current registration and access details from the Bundestag visitor service, so do not build the whole two-hour window around a casual walk-in assumption.

items.q: Can I visit Museum Island in 2 hours?
items.a: Use 2 hours for the Museum Island setting plus one specific museum reason, not all five museums. If you have no timed entry and no single collection in mind, walk the island, the river edge and Lustgarten first, then save a museum interior for a longer visit.

items.q: Is the Berliner Dom worth seeing if I do not go inside?
items.a: Yes. The dome, riverside setting and Lustgarten approach make it a meaningful exterior landmark. Go inside only when the current visitor information, service schedule and your own interest make it the one interior commitment for that window.
